correctness.rationale: The local same-colour-neighbor predicate is equivalent to a cubic 2-cut, and the 16-state trace counts all valid binary colourings. The positive and negative seam-swap blocks have integer-verified characteristic polynomials x^4(x^2+2)(x^4-3x^3-x^2+2) and x^4(x^2-x+1), proving both recurrences and the six-periodic difference. Removal of the two constant colourings and division by global complement gives precisely the unordered, nonempty cuts. A separate direct graph enumerator checks n=3..8 and an exhaustive seam bijection plus recurrences check extra boundaries. The proof is all-n, not an extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The precise new claim is the two all-parameter exact counts and their bounded six-periodic difference for unordered degree-two cuts in cyclic prisms versus Möbius ladders. Lopez-Bonilla, Allagan and Morgan already derive ordinary and twisted transfer traces for proper chromatic polynomials of these same graph families, but those count proper colourings and do not yield the nonproper same-colour-neighbor 2-cut counts. Gomes and Sau treat general d-cut algorithms and existence, not the two exact enumerators. Kwon, Park and Sano, and Rotenberg, Rutschmann and Thomassen, treat the stricter two-total-dominating-set condition, which implies a degree-two cut on cubic graphs but does not determine its count. Published calculations of six-periodic colorings, independent sets and two-cycle dynamics on similar graph families have different predicates; their conclusions do not imply this count. Several targeted source searches found no direct equivalent; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Search and the inspected papers cannot establish global historical uniqueness; some indexing of older enumerations may be incomplete.
Closest published results on related local constraints were compared at statement/abstract level, not all at full-text level; different state predicates make direct implication implausible.
Independent mathematical audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact enumeration and a structural cancellation theorem for an infinite pair of natural cubic graph families, motivated by degree-bounded cuts and local graph colouring. The seam twist changes counts by no more than two despite each family having at least 2^(n-1)-1 cuts. The combinatorial involution isolates the exceptional configurations that can detect the twist, and the recurrences allow reproducible counts for arbitrary n. These are mathematically motivated invariants, not an arbitrary finite table.
